1.title: John receives the message
1.caption: An artistic reconstruction of John on Patmos, where he received the vision.

1.title: Jesus among the lampstands
1.caption: The risen Jesus stands among the lampstands representing His churches.

2.title: Christ cares for His churches
2.caption: The lampstands picture the churches addressed by Jesus.

2.title: A message to the churches
2.caption: The stars recall the angels of the churches, addressed in these letters.

3.title: The promise of white clothing
3.caption: An illustration of the purity and belonging pictured by white clothing.

3.title: Jesus calls His people back
3.caption: A thematic illustration of Jesus, who calls Laodicea to repentance and fellowship.

4.title: Heavenly worship
4.caption: A sanctuary-themed illustration introducing worship before God’s throne.

5.title: The scroll
5.caption: A thematic scroll illustration; the chapter describes a scroll sealed with seven seals.

5.title: The Lamb is worthy
5.caption: The Lamb points to Christ, whose redeeming death is the reason for heaven’s praise.

6.title: A world in conflict
6.caption: Thematic artwork for the suffering and upheaval revealed by the seals.

6.title: White robes and hope
6.caption: The faithful receive white robes while awaiting God’s vindication.

7.title: God knows His people
7.caption: Thematic artwork of God’s people; the sealing is described in the verses beside it.

7.title: A people from every nation
7.caption: An illustration of the redeemed gathered to Christ. Compare the multitude here with 1 Thessalonians 4:16–17.

8.title: The prayers of the saints
8.caption: Incense accompanies the prayers presented before God.

8.title: The trumpets begin
8.caption: A thematic illustration of upheaval and warning, rather than a literal rendering of each trumpet.

9.title: Warnings and distress
9.caption: Thematic imagery of crisis introduces the fifth and sixth trumpets.

10.title: A heavenly messenger
10.caption: A thematic illustration of John receiving a heavenly message.

10.title: Receive the little book
10.caption: The scroll introduces the message John is told to receive and proclaim.

11.title: The temple and worshippers
11.caption: Sanctuary imagery introduces the measuring scene.

11.title: The two witnesses
11.caption: Scripture represented by a scroll recalls the Adventist interpretation of the witnesses as the Old and New Testaments.

12.title: The woman clothed with the sun
12.caption: An illustration of the woman in John’s vision.

12.title: The dragon is cast down
12.caption: The dragon represents Satan, as the chapter explicitly explains.

13.title: The first beast · Papal power
13.caption: Vatican architecture accompanies this study’s identification of the first beast with papal religious-political power. The explanation concerns a system and its actions, not individual Catholics.

13.title: The second beast · America
13.caption: The US Capitol accompanies this study’s identification of the second beast with the United States in a coercive religious role. The passage describes the beast’s actions without naming America.

14.title: With the Lamb
14.caption: The Lamb stands at the centre of the faithful people’s hope.

14.title: The earth’s harvest
14.caption: Artwork of Christ’s return introduces the harvest vision and its completion of earth’s story.

15.title: Before the last plagues
15.caption: A heavenly sanctuary illustration introduces the setting of the seven angels.

15.title: The victorious give praise
15.caption: Thematic artwork of the redeemed accompanies the song of Moses and the Lamb.

16.title: First plague · Painful sores
16.caption: An imagined scene illustrating the sores described in verse 2.

16.title: Second plague · The sea becomes blood
16.caption: The lifeless red sea illustrates the second bowl.

16.title: Third plague · Rivers become blood
16.caption: Fresh waters turn to blood; the accompanying verses explain the judgment.

16.title: Fourth plague · Scorching heat
16.caption: Intense heat illustrates the sun’s power in the fourth bowl.

16.title: Fifth plague · Darkness
16.caption: An imagined city under darkness pictures the judgment on the beast’s kingdom.

16.title: Sixth plague · The Euphrates dries
16.caption: An imagined dried riverbed introduces the sixth bowl. The passage also describes deception and the gathering of the kings.

16.title: Seventh plague · Earthquake and hail
16.caption: An imagined scene of great hail and collapsing buildings illustrates the final bowl.

17.title: The woman called Babylon
17.caption: The symbolic woman portrays corrupt splendour and unfaithfulness in the vision.

17.title: The beast · Papal religious-political power
17.caption: Vatican imagery accompanies this study’s explanation of the beast and its alliance with religious power. The interpretation concerns systems and actions, not individual Catholics.

17.title: Paul VI Audience Hall · Interior
17.caption: This front-facing view shows the oval windows, ribbed ceiling and angled pillars that suggest a serpent’s face to some viewers. The resemblance is a visual comparison; Revelation 17 does not name this building.
17.credit: Image via Historia Arte · Manuel Chacón-Palomares · Resized for display

18.title: The fall of Babylon · Vatican imagery
18.caption: An imagined collapse using Vatican architecture to illustrate the papal connection in this historicist reading. This is not a prediction of the precise fate of these buildings; Babylon represents a wider corrupt religious-political system.

18.title: The end of Babylon’s power
18.caption: The symbolic woman recalls the system whose corruption and violence are exposed by this chapter.

19.title: The marriage of the Lamb
19.caption: Fine linen is associated with the righteousness of the saints in verse 8.

19.title: The returning King
19.caption: An artistic vision of Jesus’ visible return. Read the Rider’s titles and symbolic description beside it.

20.title: The thousand years
20.caption: Thematic artwork introduces the millennium and Christ’s reign.

20.title: Resurrection and reunion
20.caption: An illustration of the redeemed meeting Jesus, connecting the first resurrection with 1 Thessalonians 4:16–17.

21.title: All things made new
21.caption: An artistic vision of renewed creation and life with God.

21.title: The bride, the holy city
21.caption: A conceptual illustration of New Jerusalem, shown as the Lamb’s bride.

22.title: Life restored
22.caption: A thematic illustration of the world made new, where the curse is gone.

22.title: Come, Lord Jesus
22.caption: An illustration of the hope of Christ’s return and gathering His people.
